intro: An agent can follow an instruction hidden in a document instead of its user's request. AgentDrift provides labeled synthetic examples for studying where that happens. Its most useful lesson for a builder is how an impressive evaluation score can come from recognizing the test data.
mechanism: AgentDrift labels individual steps of synthetic tool-use histories. It supplies evaluation data, not a proven protective layer. Some examples contain attacks; others contain suspicious-looking but legitimate content.
takeaway: Treat this as an evaluation resource. The lookup result exposes a shortcut, while recall measures attacks caught by one simple detector. Those are different questions. One weak detector also does not prove that every non-sequential approach must fail.

comparisons.title: Accuracy that comes from a shortcut
comparisons.definition: Binary accuracy counts correctly classified attacked and non-attacked histories.
comparisons.scope: Default 1,881-trajectory test split. The lookup reuses world identities seen in training.
comparisons.caveat: This is leakage evidence, not a 30-point security improvement. A detector must be evaluated with identity shortcuts controlled.

comparisons.title: Attack recall is a different denominator
comparisons.definition: Recall is the share of actual attacks detected. Here the baseline catches 460 of 831.
comparisons.scope: Single held-out test evaluation of a six-feature logistic regression.
comparisons.caveat: This is not overall accuracy. The partial-hijack subset has 8.2% recall, and benign histories have a 10.5% false-alarm rate.

plan.scenario: Possible product use: an assistant that reads customer uploads or fetched web pages before calling your APIs.
plan.change: Use the dataset to challenge your existing checks offline. Keep tools mocked so that a test cannot send messages, alter records, or expose real customer data.
plan.baseline: Your current detector against a small human-reviewed set. Separate real attack success, resisted attacks, and legitimate content that looks suspicious.
steps: Fetch the official dataset linked by the paper, record its version and license, and inspect the label definitions. Start with a small sample of attacked and legitimate histories that resemble your workflow.
Split by world identity so the same world cannot appear in training and evaluation. Keep product test examples separate from any detector tuning. Check for repeated templates and names.
Replay the held-out cases through your existing checks with mocked tools. Record the exact step flagged, missed successful attacks, and legitimate actions blocked.
Only then compare a candidate detection change on the same cases. Manually review disagreements and repeat with held-out examples from your own agent before enabling enforcement.
plan.measure: Attack recall, false-positive rate on legitimate tasks, delay until detection, review burden, and detector cost. Keep denominators and attack types visible instead of reporting one overall score.
plan.decision: Keep a change only if it catches more consequential attacks within your preselected false-alarm and latency limits. Synthetic benchmark performance alone is not evidence that a production agent is protected.
